competitors.title: The Agentic Commerce Protocol Stack: UCP, ACP, AP2, MCP, A2A Explained
key_points: Five protocols organized into three layers: Foundation (MCP, A2A), Commerce (UCP, ACP), Payment (AP2), Settlement (x402 optional)
MCP handles tool integration (agent-to-tool), A2A handles agent communication (agent-to-agent)
UCP is decentralized discovery (Google+Shopify), ACP is platform-mediated (OpenAI+Stripe)
AP2 uses Verifiable Digital Credentials (VDCs) with three mandate types: Intent, Cart, Payment
Recommended implementation order: MCP foundation -> ACP checkout -> UCP manifest -> A2A Agent Card -> AP2 mandates -> x402
Shopify ships MCP endpoints on every store by default; PayPal, Visa, Marqeta, Worldpay have MCP servers
UCP has 20+ retail/payment partners; AP2 has 60+ partners; A2A has 150+ organizations

competitors.title: MCP vs A2A vs AP2 vs UCP vs ACP: The Complete Guide to Agentic Commerce Protocols (2026)
key_points: Five-layer protocol map: Identity/Trust, Payment Authorization, Commerce Workflow, Agent-to-Agent, Tool/Data Access

angles: The protocol stack is layered, not competitive — merchants implement layers, not pick winners
UCP vs ACP is the only real contest, and it's tilting decisively toward UCP (lower cost, Linux Foundation governance, broader partner ecosystem)
Discovery-first model means catalog quality and structured data matter more than protocol choice
The identity/trust layer is wide open — four competing standards with no winner yet, creating uncertainty for 2027 planning
x402 is overkill for retail but transformative for agent-to-agent microtransactions and API monetization
Shopify is uniquely positioned across the entire stack — MCP endpoints, UCP co-development, ACP support, Agentic Storefronts
Zero interoperability means dual-syndication (ACP + UCP) is the 2026 baseline for maximum AI surface coverage
Payment protocol selection can wait until Q4 2026 — existing PSPs handle transactions in the discovery-first model
